evidence.claim: IEA reported global data-centre electricity use grew 17% in 2025 and that capex by five large technology companies exceeded $400 billion in 2025, with a further 75% increase expected in 2026.
evidence.source_title: Data centre electricity use surged in 2025, even with tightening bottlenecks driving a scramble for solutions

evidence.claim: EIA's May 2026 Short-Term Energy Outlook said the commercial sector, including data centers, is the most significant source of U.S. electricity demand growth, with electricity sales forecast to grow 2.2% in 2026 and 5.3% in 2027.
evidence.source_title: Short-Term Energy Outlook - Electricity, coal, renewables, and emissions

evidence.claim: Powell Industries reported backlog of $1.8 billion as of March 31, 2026, up 33%, and disclosed an additional post-quarter data-center order exceeding $400 million tied to a behind-the-meter on-site generation design.
evidence.source_title: Powell Industries Announces Second Quarter Fiscal 2026 Results

evidence.claim: IES Holdings reported fiscal Q2 2026 Infrastructure Solutions revenue of $192.4 million, up 64% year over year, driven by strong demand in custom engineered solutions primarily in the data-center end market.
evidence.source_title: IES Holdings Reports Fiscal 2026 Second Quarter Results

evidence.claim: Hammond Power Solutions reported Q1 2026 backlog up 94.6% versus Q1 2025, citing large projects largely driven by data-centre activity.
evidence.source_title: Hammond Power Solutions Reports First Quarter 2026 Financial Results

evidence.claim: nVent announced the acquisition of Avail Infrastructure Solutions' Electrical Products Group, adding enclosures, switchgear, and bus systems used in power utilities and data centers.
evidence.source_title: nVent to Acquire the Electrical Products Group Business of Avail Infrastructure Solutions

evidence.claim: The U.S. Department of Energy Office of Electricity 2026 strategic plan identifies high-voltage transformers, large-scale energy storage, and grid power electronics as focus areas for reliability and modernization.
evidence.source_title: Office of Electricity Strategic Plan March 2026

memory_update.content: For New Hotspots / AI data-center power bottlenecks, prioritize backlog-validated custom electrical equipment and execution-capacity suppliers over high-attention mega-cap reference leaders.

memory_update.reason: Highest combination of demand durability, bottleneck proximity, evidence quality, public-market mapping, and falsifiable near-term verification path.
Underfollowed second-order candidates with potentially high mispricing, but require stronger evidence linking demand to data-center-driven grid and transformer supply-chain constraints.
Use as demand and pricing-check anchors rather than primary underfollowed alpha candidates.
Micro-cap speculative shadow; must prove actual data-center or grid-constrained industrial revenue before advancing beyond Layer 3.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether backlog growth is durable and data-center driven versus one-off mega projects; whether gross margin holds as Powell scales complex custom projects; whether the $400 million-plus data-center order converts without cancellations or scope changes.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need project-level backlog composition, customer concentration, cancellation terms, delivery timing, and gross-margin sensitivity as large custom projects ramp.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Powell has the cleanest Serenity-style mapping in this chunk: custom-engineered medium-voltage switchgear and power-distribution systems sit directly on the critical path for data-center energization. Cached Layer 2 evidence shows backlog of $1.8 billion as of March 31, 2026, up 33%, plus a post-quarter data-center order exceeding $400 million tied to behind-the-meter on-site generation design. This combines demand durability, bottleneck severity, public-market purity, and falsifiable backlog conversion evidence.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Historically screened as a cyclical industrial or energy electrical-equipment company rather than an AI infrastructure bottleneck supplier. The AI signal is embedded in backlog, project language, and medium-voltage switchgear rather than obvious AI sector labels.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether backlog is enforceable and margin-accretive, since some disclosed backlog may include signed agreements and letters of intent without enforceable obligations before work starts; also verify data-center customer concentration and labor availability.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need clearer split of signed backlog versus letters of intent, hyperscale customer concentration, labor availability, project execution risk, and segment margin durability.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: IES is a strong second-order bottleneck candidate because data-center electrical installation, communications infrastructure, prefabrication, commissioning, and skilled field labor can constrain energization even when equipment is available. Cached Layer 2 evidence shows fiscal Q2 2026 Infrastructure Solutions revenue of $192.4 million, up 64% year over year, driven primarily by data-center custom engineered solutions.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Often categorized as an electrical contractor or mixed services company, which can hide scarce skilled-labor and engineered-solutions exposure to hyperscale data-center buildout.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: How much backlog is true hyperscale/data-center transformer demand versus broader commercial, EV, utility, or distribution-channel stocking; verify U.S. OTC liquidity, Mexico capacity ramp, and tariff or steel/aluminum margin effects.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need segment/customer evidence tying backlog to data centers, plus capacity expansion timing, pricing pass-through, input-cost sensitivity, and liquidity profile.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Hammond has direct exposure to dry-type and custom transformers, a high-signal bottleneck node for AI/data-center power and broader electrification. Cached Layer 2 evidence shows Q1 2026 backlog up 94.6% versus Q1 2025, with management citing large projects largely driven by data-centre activity. It ranks slightly below Powell because its U.S. OTC structure, market-cap uncertainty, and backlog composition require more verification.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Primary listing is Canadian and U.S. exposure is via OTC, causing many U.S.-centric AI infrastructure and electrical-equipment screens to miss it despite direct transformer exposure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether order growth is tied to U.S. grid upgrades for data-center load pockets rather than normal utility replacement cycles or international demand; check U.S. Energy segment growth, backlog, customer concentration, and connector/line-hardware capacity.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need direct evidence connecting PLPC demand to data-center-driven utility upgrades instead of normal utility maintenance, replacement cycles, or non-U.S. projects.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: PLPC is a classic underfollowed second-order Serenity candidate: not the obvious transformer or switchgear name, but potentially exposed to substation connectors, T&D line hardware, and grid-interconnection upgrades required around data-center load pockets. The thesis is less proven than Powell, IES, or Hammond, but the hidden supply-chain signal and testability are attractive.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Small niche industrial with messy labels. The AI angle is not branded as data-center equipment but sits one step upstream in utility, substation, connector, and line-hardware infrastructure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether transformer-core capacity is actually sold into U.S. utility or data-center transformer OEMs; verify electrical-steel revenue, transformer-core utilization, customer concentration, pricing pass-through, and capex timing for Canada transformer-core expansion.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need revenue mix, customer evidence, transformer OEM exposure, capacity-utilization data, and proof that transformer-core demand is an actual bottleneck rather than a generic electrification tailwind.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Worthington Steel is an upstream materials candidate tied to electrical steel laminations and transformer cores. If transformer scarcity is partly constrained by cores, laminations, or electrical steel processing capacity, WS may be one or two steps upstream from the visible AI power bottleneck. It scores highly for underfollowed discovery and mispricing potential but lower for evidence quality and purity until customer and revenue linkage are proven.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Usually screened as a steel processor, so electrical-steel and transformer-core exposure can be hidden inside broad industrial-materials labels.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Post-acquisition revenue growth, backlog conversion, margin contribution, and whether data-center and utility customers are driving incremental capacity additions in Systems Protection.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need post-acquisition segment disclosure showing how much incremental growth, backlog, and margin are tied to data-center or utility power demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: nVent is a useful reference-plus candidate because the Avail Electrical Products Group acquisition adds switchgear, bus systems, enclosures, and control-building exposure relevant to utility and data-center power systems. It is less pure and less underfollowed than the top-ranked names, but it helps validate demand in the broader electrical protection and systems layer.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: The parent company is not especially underfollowed, but the Avail Electrical Products Group exposure can be hidden inside nVent's broader connection, protection, and enclosures label rather than screened as pure AI-power equipment.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether data-center orders continue converting into revenue without margin dilution from capacity additions, labor constraints, or component shortages; track Electrical Americas backlog, book-to-bill, and lead-time commentary.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Because the company is broad and well-followed, the main gap is not demand validation but whether incremental data-center upside is already priced and whether smaller suppliers offer cleaner hidden exposure.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Eaton is not an underfollowed discovery, but it remains a key reference leader for the electrical infrastructure bottleneck. Its data-center orders, Electrical Americas backlog, book-to-bill, lead-time commentary, and margin conversion can validate whether demand remains strong across the power-distribution chain.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included as a reference anchor so smaller suppliers can be compared against a confirmed demand signal rather than social-media narratives.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether gas turbine backlog, slot reservations, and grid-equipment demand remain tied to actual data-center power projects rather than broad utility replacement; monitor order quality, cancellation risk, and margin conversion.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need separation of data-center-related orders from broader utility, grid replacement, and global power-generation demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: GE Vernova is a high-signal reference leader for the migration of AI/data-center demand into generation capacity, gas turbines, grid equipment, and behind-the-meter power. It is not an underfollowed candidate and is less pure because it spans multiple power markets, but its gas turbine slot reservations, grid-equipment orders, and backlog commentary can validate the behind-the-meter generation thesis.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included because its guidance and backlog commentary validate that AI/data-center demand is flowing into broader power-generation and grid-infrastructure equipment.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether actual revenue is coming from data centers or grid-constrained industrial customers, not only EV charging, general backup-power markets, or unrelated distributed-power demand.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need customer names, order disclosures, backlog, segment revenue, and project evidence tying the business to data-center, hyperscale, or AI-power demand. Without that, this remains speculative.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Pioneer Power is retained only as a speculative shadow candidate. Backup power, distributed power systems, and grid-constrained industrial customers could intersect with AI/data-center power constraints, but the cached candidate text does not provide enough evidence that actual revenue is coming from data centers or AI-related grid constraints.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Micro-cap and niche power-equipment profile may be overlooked by broad AI infrastructure screens, but this is not yet a validated hidden supply-chain signal.

summary: Layer 3 ranking prioritizes candidates closest to durable AI/data-center power bottlenecks with observable backlog, order, capacity, or customer-validation evidence. Highest priority goes to niche electrical-equipment and execution-capacity names where AI infrastructure demand appears in backlog or segment growth but is not fully captured by simple sector labels. Reference mega-caps are retained only as validation anchors, not as the main alpha hunt. Speculative shadow names require stronger proof of actual data-center revenue before advancing.
